qns_content.text: Which carboxylic acid is prepared by oxidation of a primary alcohol?

text_solutions: Oxidation of ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, with a strong oxidizing agent yields acetic acid (\( \ce{CH3COOH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound forms a violet color with neutral \( \ce{FeCl3} \) when derived from benzoic acid?

text_solutions: Benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) itself doesn’t react, but its derivatives like salicylic acid (not directly in PDF) don’t fit; the question stretches to carboxylic acid properties, implying a misstep. Corrected to benzoic acid’s lack of reaction, but phenol-like context gives violet with \( \ce{FeCl3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the final product when hexan-2-one undergoes Clemmensen reduction?

text_solutions: Clemmensen reduction (\( \ce{Zn(Hg), HCl} \)) converts hexan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) to hexane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound yields only methanal upon ozonolysis of its alkene precursor?

text_solutions: Ethene (\( \ce{CH2=CH2} \)) undergoes ozonolysis to form two molecules of methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)), the only carbonyl product.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 3-methylbutanal undergoes Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: 3-Methylbutanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming 3-methylbutanol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH2OH} \)) and 3-methylbutanoate.

qns_content.text: What is the product when methanal reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Cannizzaro reaction?

text_solutions: Methanal (\( \ce{HCHO} \)) lacks α-hydrogens, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, forming methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) and formate ion.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when acetone reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \) followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \), adding a methyl group to the carbonyl carbon. Hydrolysis yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which test gives a yellow precipitate with pentan-2-one?

text_solutions: The iodoform test (\( \ce{I2, NaOH} \)) is positive for compounds with a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group, like pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)), forming \( \ce{CHI3} \).

qns_content.text: How can ethanal be converted to but-2-enal?

text_solutions: Ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) undergoes aldol condensation with base, forming 3-hydroxybutanal, which dehydrates to but-2-enal (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Arrange in increasing order of boiling points: Ethanal, Ethanol, Acetone.

text_solutions: Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces: Acetone (weak dipole-dipole) < Ethanal (stronger dipole-dipole) < Ethanol (H-bonding).

qns_content.text: Which compound forms a six-carbon ketone when its calcium salt is heated?

text_solutions: Calcium butanoate (\( \ce{(CH3CH2CH2COO)2Ca} \)) from butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) decarboxylates to form heptan-4-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCH2CH2CH3} \)), a six-carbon ketone.

qns_content.text: Which of the following aldehydes gives a positive iodoform test?

text_solutions: The iodoform test is positive for compounds with a \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)-} \) or \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group. Ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) forms \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)I} \) with iodine and base, giving a yellow precipitate.

qns_content.text: Which compound gives a positive Fehling’s test but not an iodoform test?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) is an aliphatic aldehyde (positive Fehling’s test) but lacks a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group (negative iodoform test).

qns_content.text: What is the product when acetophenone is oxidized with \( \ce{SeO2} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SeO2} \) oxidizes the α-carbon of ketones. Acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) forms phenylglyoxal (\( \ce{C6H5COCHO} \)).

qns_content.text: Which method is used to prepare ketones from carboxylic acids?

text_solutions: Heating calcium salts of carboxylic acids (e.g., calcium acetate) decarboxylates them to form ketones like acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when ethanoic acid is heated with calcium hydroxide?

text_solutions: Heating the calcium salt of ethanoic acid (\( \ce{(CH3COO)2Ca} \)) decarboxylates it to form acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CHO)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the aldehyde group has 4 carbons (butanal), with a methyl group on C-2: 2-methylbutanal.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (propanoic acid in IUPAC) is historically called propionic acid in common nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which test gives a yellow precipitate with butan-2-one?

text_solutions: The iodoform test (\( \ce{I2, NaOH} \)) is positive for compounds with a \( \ce{CH3C=O} \) group, like butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)), forming \( \ce{CHI3} \).

qns_content.text: Which carboxylic acid has the highest solubility in water among the following?

text_solutions: Solubility decreases with chain length due to hydrophobic effects. Methanoic acid (\( \ce{HCOOH} \)) has the shortest chain and highest solubility.

qns_content.text: Which compound evolves \( \ce{CO2} \) when its calcium salt is heated with calcium methanoate?

text_solutions: Pentanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH} \)) forms calcium pentanoate, which, when heated with calcium methanoate (\( \ce{(HCOO)2Ca} \)), yields pentanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO} \)) and \( \ce{CO2} \).
